extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, actors, theatre/masque/puppet-producers and educated theatre-going public
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative criteria for theatrical entertainments (opera, masque, puppet-show, stage spectacles) — covering acting, staging, scenic mechanics, use of animals, language, and audience expectation. Grounded in early-18th-century theatrical criticism but applicable to stagecraft and dramatic writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of physical action and facial expression in acting
rubrics_metrics.description: Could they make the same use of their Arms and Legs, and inform their Faces with as significant Looks and Passions, how glorious would an English Tragedy appear with that action which is capable of giving a Dignity to the forced Thoughts, cold Conceits, and unnatural Expressions of an Italian Opera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors should employ their bodies and faces to convey meaning and passion; physicality and expressive looks lend dignity and render dialogue and thought credible. The passage praises Nicolini's power of action and suggests English tragedians would benefit from similar use of limbs and facial expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve character consistency in masquerade/role-playing
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a kind of acting to go in Masquerade, and a Man should be able to say or do things proper for the Dress in which he appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maskers must maintain their adopted character in speech and behavior; costume should be matched by appropriate language and conduct. The essay gives examples of mismatches (rakes dressed as Roman senators, philosophers speechless in a masque) and urges reading source romances (Arcadia) to inhabit roles properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage audience expectations; avoid over‑promising
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr Powell wisely forbearing to give his Company a Bill of Fare before-hand, every Scene is new and unexpected; whereas the Undertakers of the Hay-Market, having raised too great an Expectation in their printed Opera, very much disappointed their Audience on the Stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing or promising spectacles that cannot be delivered; surprise can be an advantage, while printed/programmed expectations create disappointment. The advice applies to producers and writers when setting expectations for an audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenic and mechanical consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Undertakers forgetting to change their Side-Scenes, we were presented with a Prospect of the Ocean in the midst of a delightful Grove; and tho' the Gentlemen on the Stage had very much contributed to the Beauty of the Grove, by walking up and down between the Trees, I must own I was not a little astonished to see a well-dressed young Fellow in a full-bottomed Wigg, appear in the Midst of the Sea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain unity and coherence in scenery and scene changes; avoid jarring visual inconsistencies that break audience immersion. Stage mechanics (scene shifts, side-scenes) must be properly managed to preserve the illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and proportion of stage effects
rubrics_metrics.description: He flash'd out his Rosin in such just Proportions, and in such due Time, that I could not forbear conceiving Hopes of his being one Day a most excellent Player. I saw, indeed, but Two things wanting to render his whole Action compleat, I mean the keeping his Head a little lower, and hiding his Candle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special effects (fire, smoke, thunder, lightning, mechanical dragons) must be used with correct timing and in the right measure; small technical details (positioning, concealing instruments) matter to finish the effect and preserve realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline and management of animals on stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sparrows and Chaffinches at the Hay-Market fly as yet very irregularly over the Stage ... whereas Mr Powell has so well disciplined his Pig, that in the first Scene he and Punch dance a Minuet together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When animals are used as performers, they must be trained and controlled so they perform their parts and do not disrupt the action; successful animal performances enhance the spectacle, while undisciplined ones create chaos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the audience's native language for accessibility and wit
rubrics_metrics.description: As the Wit in both Pieces are equal, I must prefer the Performance of Mr Powell, because it is in our own Language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performances in the audience's native language are preferable because they communicate wit, nuance, and moral meaning more effectively to the public. Language choice affects accessibility and enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain dignity of lofty roles; avoid pandering to vulgar taste
rubrics_metrics.description: It gives me a just Indignation, to see a Person whose Action gives new Majesty to Kings, Resolution to Heroes, and Softness to Lovers, thus sinking from the Greatness of his Behaviour, and degraded into the Character of the London Prentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists and actors should not lower the dignity of great roles by adopting coarse or vulgar mannerisms to please popular tastes; noble action and elevated performance should be preserved to sustain the art's moral and aesthetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and plausibility in staged spectacles
rubrics_metrics.description: I have made it my Business to examine whether this pretended Lion is really the Savage he appears to be, or only a Counterfeit ... It has been observed ... that the Lion has changed his manner of Acting twice or thrice since his first Appearance; which will not seem strange, when I acquaint my Reader that the Lion has been changed upon the Audience three several times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectacles must strive for apparent authenticity; sham or obviously counterfeit effects (or performers changed to suit convenience) undermine the performance. The essay examines audience rumours and stresses the need for believable presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate vocal casting for heroic roles
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Squeak of their Voices the Heroes of each are Eunuchs; and as the Wit in both Pieces are equal, I must prefer the Performance of Mr Powell, because it is in our own Language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocal quality should suit character type; heroic roles require suitable, robust voices—casting should avoid voices that undermine a character's stature or credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temper writing about ghosts and apparitions with reason and religion
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to arm our selves against them by the Dictates of Reason and Religion, 'to pull the old Woman out of our Hearts' ... For my own Part, I am apt to join in Opinion with those who believe that all the Regions of Nature swarm with Spirits ... but instead of terrifying my self with such a Notion, I am wonderfully pleased to think that I am always engaged with such an innumerable Society ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating supernatural subjects, writers should avoid needlessly terrifying readers; use reason, moral grounding, or religious perspective to moderate fear and to frame such material in a way that uplifts rather than merely shocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict characters (esp. women) beyond superficial ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: I have often reflected ... on this unaccountable Humour in Woman-kind, of being smitten with every thing that is showy and superficial ... they consider only the Drapery of the Species, and never cast away a Thought on those Ornaments of the Mind, that make Persons Illustrious in themselves, and Useful to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrayals should emphasize inner virtues, judgment, and domestic harmony rather than superficial finery and public show; true happiness arises from private friendship and domestic good sense, not pomp and noise. This serves as moral guidance for character development and themes.
